message.content: The implementation is correct; two of my test expectations were wrong. With empty columns, the header plus one record per row yields three CRLF records; and `(1, 2)` contains a comma so RFC 4180 minimal quoting requires quotes. Fixing my tests:
message.reasoning_content:
Two test failures:
1. test_empty_columns_no_header: with empty columns, each row writes a record — actually with empty cols, csv.writer.writerow([]) writes just the terminator "
". Plus header writes "
". So 2 rows + 1 header = 3 "
". My test expected 2. What's the correct spec? "Return a str containing CSV header then one record per row, in that order." With empty columns, header is an empty record → "
", and one record per row → "
" each. So 3 is correct; fix my test.

2. test_non_string_values_str: tuple "(1, 2)" contains no comma, so minimal quoting doesn't quote it. Actually "(1, 2)" does contain a comma... wait, "(1, 2)" contains ", " — yes it has a comma! So csv quotes it: "(1, 2)". Right, minimal quoting quotes fields containing commas. My expected value was wrong. Fix the test to expect quoting.
